title: Extracting Governing Equations from Latent Dynamics via Multi-View Contrastive Learning
claim: Latent dynamics seen only through noisy high-dimensional views can be recovered by contrasting temporally aligned embeddings across views.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; 3D latent-to-observation stack feeding a contrastive-loss box
description: Panel (a) shows a 3D perspective scene. At the top, a latent trajectory with chaotic oscillations lies on translucent teal and purple planes, labeled x_t, x_t^(1) and x_t^(2), with the flow field f: X→X. A red arrow labeled g: R^d→R^D points down to two stacked strips of black-and-white noisy neuron-like raster data (views a and b, y_t^a and y_t^b). Colored vertical lines mark an anchor (blue), a positive (red) and negatives (green). A black arrow labeled h: R^D→R^d leads to panel (b). Panel (b) is a rounded gray box titled 'multi-view temporal contrastive learning'. It has a color legend (anchor, positive, negatives), the formula φ = −||u−v||², a small 3D embedding scatter with arrows from the anchor to a positive and to negatives, and a wavy learned trajectory with the flow map f̂ and the points t*, t+ and t−. The eye goes first to the 3D latent trajectory.
caption: Graphical overview. (a) We consider a latent dynamical system (top) that evolves according to an unknown dynamics f : X 7→X. We observe the system via a non-linear mixing-channel g : Rd 7→RD that produces noisy high-dimensional observations ya
abstract: Identifying latent dynamical systems from noisy, high-dimensional measurements is a central problem at the intersection of representation learning, system identification, and scientific discovery. We present DYSCO, a multi-view temporal contrastive learning algorithm that jointly recovers latent trajectories and the governing dynamics from such observations, by leveraging multiple independent noisy views of the same underlying process to disentangle signal from noise. By parameterizing the dynamics in a structured functional basis, our framework further enables symbolic recovery of the governing equations within an affine gauge. We offer theoretical guarantees for strong identification up to an affine indeterminacy, extending prior identifiability results to the realistic setting of noisy nonlinear observations. Empirically, we demonstrate accurate recovery of both latent trajectories and flow fields across a diverse set of dynamical regimes (e.g., chaotic, oscillatory, and metastable) under both Gaussian and Poisson observation noise, the latter being particularly relevant for neural recordings.
